mechanism_narrative: A higher current federal funds rate directly increases the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to lower expected S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate (indicating a monetary tightening coupled with labor market weakness) creates a 'stagflationary' risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise simultaneously (each by more than 0.2pp in 3 months), the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of real GDP (GDPC1 above 16500 billion) signals a strong economy, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 is above 16500, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL rising more than 0.5 percentage points over three months) signals an impending monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong industrial production level (INDPRO above 105) signals robust manufacturing activity, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO is above 105, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint strength in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and INDPRO are above their 1-year moving averages, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential sales (RSAFS falling below 450000 million) signals weakening consumer demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS falls below 450000 million, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
